title: Grant creature count: bind the source-backed count at use_item -> start_effect (Horn of Valhalla rolled horn-type count; elemental vessels' single elemental)
description:
RECONCILED 2026-10-18 after the architectural boundary review of magic-item deterministic ownership. This supersedes the 2026-10-17 framing where the two differ; the original text is kept verbatim in NOTES.

This is a PRE-FREEZE engine obligation: it blocks eshyra-o9bd.14 under the user rules of 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-17. The scope is only to enforce source-backed creature MULTIPLICITY at the real use_item -> start_effect grant-binding boundary. It is not summoning interpretation.

SOURCE
- Horn of Valhalla: "The horn's type determines how many berserkers answer its summons, as well as the requirement for its use. The GM chooses the horn's type or determines it randomly." table:horn-of-valhalla rows: Silver 2d4 + 2, Brass 3d4 + 3, Bronze 4d4 + 4, Iron 5d4 + 5.
- Bowl, Brazier, Censer and Stone of commanding/controlling elementals: each prints the summoning of ONE elemental of its type, "as if you had cast the conjure elemental spell".

VERIFIED FACTS at PR #673 head 379c90f8 (still OPEN, under user review)
- validateItemGrantBinding enforces only a fixed numeric grant.count.
- The Horn grant has tableRefs [table:horn-of-valhalla] and no count.
- The four vessel grants (the elementalVessel helper in magicItemEntityGrants.ts) carry no count.
- creatureGrantLifecycleOwned requires a fixed numeric count, so these m4 entityGrant clauses stay engine-pending.
- The Elemental Gem's count:1 is the precedent for a typed single creature.
- HORN TYPE IS NOT REPRESENTED today: no variants on the record, and no initial-state procedure on the instance. It will be represented per the decision below.

DETERMINISTIC COMMITMENT
1. Vessels: type count 1 faithfully in the curated spec. The binder already enforces fixed counts.
2. Horn: bind to the specific item use a count that the ENGINE rolled from the dice of that instance's horn type. Refuse a bind whose linked-actor count differs from that roll, or whose roll is not the engine roll attributed to that use (an unrelated or caller-supplied number).
3. Preserve what already exists: actor identity, grant identity, variant restrictions, ownership validation, bind credits and consumption receipts.

RETAINED BY THE DM: the horn type where the GM chooses it; whether the user meets the requirement, and therefore whether the berserkers are hostile or friendly; control, disposition, placement and combat decisions.

DECIDED 2026-10-18 (user): option (a).
- Horn type is a PERSISTENT property of the specific item instance. It is established once, when the item enters play (or when a previously unknown type is established), by DM choice or by deterministic random selection.
- Prefer the existing source-backed magic-item variantId mechanism, if it faithfully represents the four horn types (Silver, Brass, Bronze, Iron). Introduce no separate storage mechanism without a demonstrated need.
- Each activation rolls the count of that type's row through the deterministic engine, bound to that specific use.
- The type is NEVER reselected on activation.

NOT REQUIRED: generalized deterministic summoning; placement or geometry; deterministic requirement (proficiency) checking; hostility selection; a dice-count expression language beyond the four printed rows.

DEPENDENCY: this bead edits the ownership predicate introduced by PR #673, so it depends on eshyra-c58j.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Source requirement: Horn count = the rolled dice of the instance's horn-type row; vessel count = 1. Both are traced to printed text in the curated spec.
2. Horn type (decided 2026-10-18, option (a)):
   - It is a persistent per-instance property, established once (DM choice or deterministic random selection), preferably through the existing magic-item variantId mechanism. If variantId cannot faithfully represent the four horn types, surface that specific limitation before adding any other storage.
   - It is never reselected on activation; an activation reads the instance's established type.
3. Engine commitment:
   - The Horn count roll is made by the engine and bound durably and attributably to that item use, and it is replay-safe.
   - start_effect refuses a count mismatch.
   - start_effect refuses a roll that is not attributable to that use.
   - Grant identity, variant admission, ownership, bind credit and receipt checks are unchanged.
4. creatureGrantLifecycleOwned admits a rolled count only through this binding; the fixed-count rule is unchanged elsewhere. The vessels are certified for COUNT only; their c1-uses F5 hook is eshyra-7gkh.
5. Truthful readiness: no operation becomes ready unless every other blocking clause on it is also resolved (vessels: eshyra-7gkh).
6. Minimum permanent evidence, on the real unmodified pack with no readiness waiver:
   - One Horn bind accepted with the engine-rolled count, refused for a mismatched count, and refused for an unrelated roll.
   - One vessel bind accepted for one elemental and refused for two.
   - The regenerated pack and its thaw note, per docs/importer-fix-protocol.md.
   - No per-horn-type fixture matrix, unless the horn-type decision creates distinct code paths.
7. Not required: see NOT REQUIRED in the description.
8. The olc5 stop condition (user, 2026-10-12) applies: surface to the user if count verification cannot cheaply distinguish faithful from unfaithful.
